items.readable_text:
Content:
To divide one complex number by another, we set up a fraction and then multiply both the numerator and the denominator by the complex conjugate of the denominator.

Content:
For example, to divide [MATH: 2 - \textrm{i}] by [MATH: 1 + 3\textrm{i},] we start by setting up a fraction:
[MATH: \dfrac {2 - \textrm{i}} {1 + 3\textrm{i}}]

Content:
The denominator is [MATH: 1 + 3\textrm{i}] and its conjugate is [MATH: 1 - 3\textrm{i}.]

Content:
We multiply both the numerator and denominator by [MATH: 1 - 3\textrm{i},] so that the denominator turns into a real number:

Content:
[MATH: \eqalign{
\dfrac {2 - \textrm{i}} {1 + 3\textrm{i}} \cdot \dfrac {1 - 3\textrm{i}} {1 - 3\textrm{i}}
&= \dfrac {2 - 6\textrm{i} -\textrm{i} + 3\textrm{i}^2} {1 - 3\textrm{i} + 3\textrm{i} - 9\textrm{i}^2} \[5pt]
&= \dfrac {2 - 7\textrm{i} + 3(-1)} {1 - 9(-1)} \[5pt]
&= \dfrac {2 - 7\textrm{i} - 3} {1 + 9} \[5pt]
&= \dfrac {-1 - 7\textrm{i}} {10}
}]

Content:
Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form [MATH: a+b \textrm{i}\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: \eqalign{
\dfrac {-1 - 7\textrm{i}} {10} =
-\dfrac{1} {10} - \dfrac {7} {10} \textrm{i}
}]

sections.normalized_html: Express [MATH: \dfrac {4 + \textrm{i}} {1 - \textrm{i}}] in the form [MATH: a+\textrm{i}b.]

The denominator is [MATH: 1-\textrm{i}] and its conjugate is [MATH: 1+\textrm{i}.] We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by [MATH: 1+\textrm{i},] so that the denominator turns into a real number: [MATH: \eqalign{ \dfrac {4 + \textrm{i}} {1 - \textrm{i}} &=\dfrac {4 + \textrm{i}} {1 - \textrm{i}} \cdot \dfrac {1 + \textrm{i}} {1 + \textrm{i}} \[5pt] &= \dfrac {4 + 4\textrm{i} + \textrm{i} + \textrm{i}^2} {1^2 - \textrm{i}^2} \[5pt] &= \dfrac {4 + 5\textrm{i} + (-1)} {1 - (-1)} \[5pt] &= \dfrac {3 + 5\textrm{i}} {2} }]

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form [MATH: a+\textrm{i} b \mathbin{:}]

[MATH: \eqalign{ \dfrac {3 + 5\textrm{i}} {2} = \dfrac{3} {2} + \dfrac {5} {2} \textrm{i} }]

sections.normalized_html: If [MATH: z_1=3\textrm{i}] and [MATH: z_2 = 2+5\textrm{i},] then what is [MATH: z_1] divided by [MATH: z_2?]
sections.readable_text: If [MATH: z_1=3\textrm{i}] and [MATH: z_2 = 2+5\textrm{i},] then what is [MATH: z_1] divided by [MATH: z_2?]

sections.normalized_html:
First, we set up the fraction:

[MATH: \dfrac{3\textrm{i}}{2+5\textrm i}]

The denominator is [MATH: 2+5\textrm{i}] and its conjugate is [MATH: 2-5\textrm{i}.] We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by [MATH: 2-5\textrm{i},] so that the denominator turns into a real number: [MATH: \eqalign{ \dfrac {3 \textrm{i}} {2 +5\textrm{i}} &= \dfrac {3 \textrm{i}} {2 +5 \textrm{i}} \cdot \dfrac {2 -5 \textrm{i}} {2-5\textrm{i}} \[5pt] &=\dfrac {6 \textrm{i} - 15 \textrm{i}^2 } {2^2 - (5\textrm{i})^2} \[5pt] &=\dfrac {6 \textrm{i} - 15\textrm{i}^2 } {4 - 25\textrm{i}^2} \[5pt] &= \dfrac {6 \textrm{i} - 15(-1) } {4 - 25(-1)} \[5pt] &=\dfrac {6 \textrm{i} + 15 } {29} }]

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form [MATH: a+b \textrm{i}\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: \eqalign{ \dfrac {6 \textrm{i} + 15 } {29}= \dfrac{15} {29} + \dfrac {6} {29} \textrm{i} }]

sections.normalized_html: Express [MATH: \dfrac{4}{-1+2\textrm{i} }] in the form [MATH: a+\textrm{i}b.]

The denominator is [MATH: -1+2\textrm{i}] and its conjugate is [MATH: -1-2\textrm{i}.] We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by [MATH: -1-2\textrm{i},] so that the denominator turns into a real number: [MATH: \eqalign{ \dfrac {4} {-1 +2\textrm{i}} &=\dfrac {4} {-1 +2 \textrm{i}} \cdot \dfrac {-1 -2 \textrm{i}} {-1-2\textrm{i}} \[5pt] &= \dfrac {-4 - 8 \textrm{i} } {(-1)^2 - (2\textrm{i})^2} \[5pt] &= \dfrac {-4 - 8 \textrm{i} } {1 - 4\textrm{i}^2} \[5pt] &= \dfrac {-4 - 8 \textrm{i} } {1 - 4(-1)} \[5pt] &= \dfrac {-4 - 8 \textrm{i} } {5} }]

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form [MATH: a+b \textrm{i}\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: \eqalign{ \dfrac {-4 - 8 \textrm{i} } {5} = -\dfrac{4} {5} - \dfrac {8} {5} \textrm{i} }]

sections.readable_text: If [MATH: z_1 = -8-3\textrm{i}] and [MATH: z_2 = 2\textrm{i},] then what is [MATH: z_1] divided by [MATH: z_2?]

sections.normalized_html:
First, we set up the fraction:

[MATH: \dfrac {-8 - 3\textrm{i}} {2\textrm{i}}]

The denominator is the imaginary number [MATH: 2\textrm{i}.] Note that this can be written as [MATH: 0+2\textrm{i},] so the conjugate is [MATH: 0-2\textrm{i},] or simply [MATH: -2\textrm{i}.]

So, we multiply both the numerator and the denominator by [MATH: -2\textrm{i},] so that the denominator turns into a real number:

[MATH: \eqalign{ \dfrac {-8 - 3\textrm{i}} {2\textrm{i}} &= \dfrac {-8 - 3\textrm{i}} {2\textrm{i}} \cdot \dfrac {-2\textrm{i}} {-2\textrm{i}} \[5pt] &= \dfrac {16\textrm{i} + 6\textrm{i}^2} {-4\textrm{i}^2} \[5pt] &= \dfrac {16\textrm{i} + 6(-1)} {-4(-1)} \[5pt] &= \dfrac {-6 + 16\textrm{i}} {4} }]

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form [MATH: a+b \textrm{i}\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: \eqalign{ \dfrac {-6 + 16\textrm{i}} {4} &= - \dfrac{6}{4} + \dfrac{16}{4} \textrm{i} \[5pt] &= -\dfrac{3} {2} + 4\textrm{i} }]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
To divide one complex number by another, we set up a fraction and then multiply both the numerator and the denominator by the complex conjugate of the denominator.

Content:
For example, to divide [MATH: 2 - \textrm{i}] by [MATH: 1 + 3\textrm{i},] we start by setting up a fraction:
[MATH: \dfrac {2 - \textrm{i}} {1 + 3\textrm{i}}]

Content:
The denominator is [MATH: 1 + 3\textrm{i}] and its conjugate is [MATH: 1 - 3\textrm{i}.]

Content:
We multiply both the numerator and denominator by [MATH: 1 - 3\textrm{i},] so that the denominator turns into a real number:

Content:
[MATH: \eqalign{
\dfrac {2 - \textrm{i}} {1 + 3\textrm{i}} \cdot \dfrac {1 - 3\textrm{i}} {1 - 3\textrm{i}}
&= \dfrac {2 - 6\textrm{i} -\textrm{i} + 3\textrm{i}^2} {1 - 3\textrm{i} + 3\textrm{i} - 9\textrm{i}^2} \[5pt]
&= \dfrac {2 - 7\textrm{i} + 3(-1)} {1 - 9(-1)} \[5pt]
&= \dfrac {2 - 7\textrm{i} - 3} {1 + 9} \[5pt]
&= \dfrac {-1 - 7\textrm{i}} {10}
}]

Content:
Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form [MATH: a+b \textrm{i}\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: \eqalign{
\dfrac {-1 - 7\textrm{i}} {10} =
-\dfrac{1} {10} - \dfrac {7} {10} \textrm{i}
}]

---

Item 2 — Example: Dividing Two Complex Numbers

Example Prompt:
Express [MATH: \dfrac {4 + \textrm{i}} {1 - \textrm{i}}] in the form [MATH: a+\textrm{i}b.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
The denominator is [MATH: 1-\textrm{i}] and its conjugate is [MATH: 1+\textrm{i}.] We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by [MATH: 1+\textrm{i},] so that the denominator turns into a real number:
[MATH: \eqalign{
\dfrac {4 + \textrm{i}} {1 - \textrm{i}}
&=\dfrac {4 + \textrm{i}} {1 - \textrm{i}} \cdot \dfrac {1 + \textrm{i}} {1 + \textrm{i}} \[5pt]
&= \dfrac {4 + 4\textrm{i} + \textrm{i} + \textrm{i}^2} {1^2 - \textrm{i}^2} \[5pt]
&= \dfrac {4 + 5\textrm{i} + (-1)} {1 - (-1)} \[5pt]
&= \dfrac {3 + 5\textrm{i}} {2}
}]

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form [MATH: a+\textrm{i} b \mathbin{:}]

[MATH: \eqalign{
\dfrac {3 + 5\textrm{i}} {2} =
\dfrac{3} {2} + \dfrac {5} {2} \textrm{i}
}]

Item 5 — Example: Dividing an Imaginary Number by a Complex Number

Example Prompt:
If [MATH: z_1=3\textrm{i}] and [MATH: z_2 = 2+5\textrm{i},] then what is [MATH: z_1] divided by [MATH: z_2?]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
First, we set up the fraction:

[MATH: \dfrac{3\textrm{i}}{2+5\textrm i}]

The denominator is [MATH: 2+5\textrm{i}] and its conjugate is [MATH: 2-5\textrm{i}.] We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by [MATH: 2-5\textrm{i},] so that the denominator turns into a real number:
[MATH: \eqalign{
\dfrac {3 \textrm{i}} {2 +5\textrm{i}}
&= \dfrac {3 \textrm{i}} {2 +5 \textrm{i}} \cdot \dfrac {2 -5 \textrm{i}} {2-5\textrm{i}} \[5pt]
&=\dfrac {6 \textrm{i} - 15 \textrm{i}^2 } {2^2 - (5\textrm{i})^2} \[5pt]
&=\dfrac {6 \textrm{i} - 15\textrm{i}^2 } {4 - 25\textrm{i}^2} \[5pt]
&= \dfrac {6 \textrm{i} - 15(-1) } {4 - 25(-1)} \[5pt]
&=\dfrac {6 \textrm{i} + 15 } {29}
}]

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form [MATH: a+b \textrm{i}\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: \eqalign{
\dfrac {6 \textrm{i} + 15 } {29}=
\dfrac{15} {29} + \dfrac {6} {29} \textrm{i}
}]

Item 8 — Example: Dividing a Real Number by a Complex Number

Example Prompt:
Express [MATH: \dfrac{4}{-1+2\textrm{i} }] in the form [MATH: a+\textrm{i}b.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
The denominator is [MATH: -1+2\textrm{i}] and its conjugate is [MATH: -1-2\textrm{i}.] We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by [MATH: -1-2\textrm{i},] so that the denominator turns into a real number:
[MATH: \eqalign{
\dfrac {4} {-1 +2\textrm{i}}
&=\dfrac {4} {-1 +2 \textrm{i}} \cdot \dfrac {-1 -2 \textrm{i}} {-1-2\textrm{i}} \[5pt]
&= \dfrac {-4 - 8 \textrm{i} } {(-1)^2 - (2\textrm{i})^2} \[5pt]
&= \dfrac {-4 - 8 \textrm{i} } {1 - 4\textrm{i}^2} \[5pt]
&= \dfrac {-4 - 8 \textrm{i} } {1 - 4(-1)} \[5pt]
&= \dfrac {-4 - 8 \textrm{i} } {5}
}]

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form [MATH: a+b \textrm{i}\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: \eqalign{
\dfrac {-4 - 8 \textrm{i} } {5} =
-\dfrac{4} {5} - \dfrac {8} {5} \textrm{i}
}]

Item 11 — Example: Dividing a Complex Number by an Imaginary Number

Example Prompt:
If [MATH: z_1 = -8-3\textrm{i}] and [MATH: z_2 = 2\textrm{i},] then what is [MATH: z_1] divided by [MATH: z_2?]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
First, we set up the fraction:

[MATH: \dfrac {-8 - 3\textrm{i}} {2\textrm{i}}]

The denominator is the imaginary number [MATH: 2\textrm{i}.] Note that this can be written as [MATH: 0+2\textrm{i},] so the conjugate is [MATH: 0-2\textrm{i},] or simply [MATH: -2\textrm{i}.]

So, we multiply both the numerator and the denominator by [MATH: -2\textrm{i},] so that the denominator turns into a real number:

[MATH: \eqalign{
\dfrac {-8 - 3\textrm{i}} {2\textrm{i}}
&= \dfrac {-8 - 3\textrm{i}} {2\textrm{i}} \cdot \dfrac {-2\textrm{i}} {-2\textrm{i}} \[5pt]
&= \dfrac {16\textrm{i} + 6\textrm{i}^2} {-4\textrm{i}^2} \[5pt]
&= \dfrac {16\textrm{i} + 6(-1)} {-4(-1)} \[5pt]
&= \dfrac {-6 + 16\textrm{i}} {4}
}]

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form [MATH: a+b \textrm{i}\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: \eqalign{
\dfrac {-6 + 16\textrm{i}} {4} &= - \dfrac{6}{4} + \dfrac{16}{4} \textrm{i} \[5pt]
&= -\dfrac{3} {2} + 4\textrm{i}
}]
